finding.claim: The POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban handler swallows the 403 raised by require_admin and then calls do_ban(uid), so non-admin callers can ban arbitrary users (fail-open authorization bypass).
finding.source: Attacker-controlled uid path parameter on POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban, reachable by any caller that gets past upstream auth (a non-admin user, or anyone if g.user is unset).

trace.note: Route registered for POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with no route-level guard
require_admin(g.user) is called inside the try block
For non-admins, abort(403) raises werkzeug Forbidden, which is an Exception subclass
except Exception catches the Forbidden (or AttributeError if g.user is unset)
Logs a warning and continues instead of returning or re-raising
do_ban(uid) executes for the unauthorized caller
Returns {ok: true}, so the bypass succeeds silently

finding.guards_checked: require_admin (correct on its own: aborts when is_admin is falsy); the unban route at admin.py:24-28 calls require_admin without try/except, so its check is enforced; no decorator, before_request hook, or blueprint guard in this file. Not verifiable from the repo: the middleware that sets g.user, and the real implementation of do_ban (currently a stub with pass), so impact is conditional on do_ban.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) does raise via abort(403) for non-admins, but its result is effectively discarded: the call at admin.py:17 sits in a try whose bare `except Exception:` at admin.py:18-19 logs and falls through to do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20. No decorator, before_request hook, or blueprint guard is present in admin.py. The unban route (admin.py:26) enforces the check without try/except, which shows the intended guard.
verdict.reason: For an authenticated non-admin, require_admin raises Forbidden at admin.py:11, admin.py:18 swallows it, and admin.py:20 still calls do_ban(uid) before returning ok at admin.py:21, so the fail-open bypass is real. However, the trace is inaccurate for the case where g.user is unset: the AttributeError is caught at admin.py:18, but admin.py:19 then re-reads g.user and raises again uncaught, so do_ban never runs and the claim "or anyone if g.user is unset" is wrong. Impact also depends on do_ban, which is a stub at admin.py:31-32 and whose upstream authentication middleware is not in the repo.
